recipes.name: Grilled Chicken Burgers
ingredients_raw: 1 tablespoon seafood seasoning (such as Old Bay®)
kosher salt and ground black pepper to taste

steps.text: Lightly spray a skillet with cooking spray and heat over medium heat. Add onion and sauté until translucent, about 5 minutes. Add garlic and cook until fragrant, about 30 seconds. Add carrots, bell pepper, tomato, and mushrooms; cook and stir until tender, 5 to 7 minutes. Remove from the heat and let cool completely, about 20 minutes.
Preheat an outdoor grill for medium heat and lightly oil the grate.
Mix ground chicken and cooled vegetables together in a large bowl. Add bread crumbs, egg, seafood seasoning, salt, and pepper; mix until well combined. Form mixture into eight patties.

Cook on the preheated grill until no longer pink in the center and the juices run clear, 5 to 6 minutes per side. An instant-read thermometer inserted into the center should read at least 165 degrees F (74 degrees C).

raw_recipe.headline: Grilled Chicken Burgers
raw_recipe.description: These grilled chicken burgers are a nice change from ordinary beef hamburgers since they're made with ground chicken, vegetables, and seasonings.

review.reviewBody: This is officially my very favorite burger recipe! I've made this recipe twice. However, I have not been able to find ground chicken in my grocery store, so I made this recipe with ground turkey instead. It was fabulous! In addition, I do not have a grill, so I put about 1/4 cup of veggie oil in a skillet and cook the burgers on each side for about 4 minutes until they are golden brown. Then, I drain the burgers on paper towels and serve them with cheese on top. The veggies give the burger excellent flavor and add a lot of moisture. Very yummy and easy to make!!

I followed the recipe exactly EXCEPT I thought I had 2 lbs of ground chicken, but discovered, after I had all the other ingredients prepped, that I only had a little over a pound of chicken. Despite this, I went on, effectively including twice as many veggies as called for. I did cut back on the Old Bay seasoning because I was afraid it would be too strong.

Bottom line: it turned out great! The veggies provide good texture, and the flavor was very good. An exceptionally healthful recipe. Instead of frying the mixture as burgers, I decided to bake it in individual silicone muffin cups. Love those things! Nothing ..... and I mean nothing .... ever sticks to them. I baked them for 45 minutes at 350 degrees. 

With this approach, once cooled I could pop them in the freezer for a quick "grab & go" snack or breakfast. Just a brief warm up in the microwave, and they're ready to go. 

I'll be making these again.

These were AWESOME! I totally winged it and they still turned out great. I took bits and pieces from other reviews and made it my own. I cut out the carrots and mushrooms(since I had none on hand). Used 1/2 a large red pepper chopped, 1 small zuchini shredded, 1 onion chopped, 2lbs of ground chicken, garlic, 1 box no name seasoned crutons blended in food processor instead of breadcrumbs(I just like the texture/flavour better than breadcrumbs), onion powder, and Weber's chicken seasoning(I think this is what made the recipe). You can probably use any chicken seasoning. Oh, and some pepper and a dollop of dijon. I also used olive oil instead of cooking spray. Anyhoo, threw them on the grill for 15 min or so, and presto-probably the best homemade burger I've ever had-jam packed with flavour and the texture was perfect. Not too mushy, not too dry. I literally ate them right out of the dish after they cooled. No toppings/condiments needed.

Very good. 
Much juicer than the typical chicken or turkey burger.
 I did cut all vegetables into medium dice as chopped to me means pretty large pieces. I also cooked all veggies with the Old Bay until most all the moisture had cooked away to help ensure a firmer patty. I also did not add the egg and they held their shape very well. I did not grill them on a grill, but in grill pan with grate on non-stick foil with holes punched for draining in oven on convection broil. 
Great, brown surface, internal temp about 165. Really juicy and good!

Loved it! I made a couple changes, but I'd say the recipe is pretty darn good! I didn't have old bay spice, so I used what I had- nutmeg, ginger, allspice, ground mustard, celery salt and crushed red. My only complaint was that the burger stuck to the grill because of how sloppy it was. Fortunately it was salvageable. Next time I'll cook it a few minutes on foil to solidify. Other than that it was DELICIOUS!!! Definitely a keeper. I served with cheddar, spinach and tomato. No condiments needed! Yum!!

These are great! Freezing before grilling helps them not stick. They can go straight from your freezer to the grill, no problem. Plus you can make a big batch to freeze and only take out what you need. Lay your patties on a cookie sheet lined with wax paper and pop in the freezer. Once frozen, transfer to large ziploc bag if you wish.

These are my favorite grilled chicken burgers I make them all the time. I don't add the tomatoes. I also adjust the amount of seasonings and vegetables to my liking. I also form them into patties and put them in the refrigerator for a couple of hours for them to firm up, that way they hold up better when grilling! They are very moist and flavorful with the added vegetables!

08/23/2017 We liked these and I will make these regularly since I buy a lot of ground chicken in place of beef. (Like some others, I'm going to start grounding breast and freezing it, when it goes on sale!) I used a pound of ground chicken, halved the veges and kept the 1/2 c of bread crumbs. We used cheddar, but I think a more mild cheese might have worked better. UPDATE 06/23/2019 A few tips I found helpful with these. They are very agreeable with different additions as per your taste. I've made them with Italian bread crumbs and parmesan grated cheese. To better keep them together I formed them into patties on parchment paper, then laid them on a plate and put them in the freezer for an hour before grilling. Also, make sure to oil your grill a bit so they won't stick.
Added cayenne dry pepper and crushed corriander seems. Added Cajun seasoning. Sauted it on pan. Cooked fast. Less than 4 min on medium heat with cover. Came out good. Kids liked it too.

Made these for the 4th of July -- what a hit! People were amazed that they were so moist and tasty. It's a boatload of veggies and I was worried that they would fall apart on the grill, but all went well. I used the food processor to process boneless, skinless chicken breasts, put on disposable food gloves and went to town mixing the ingredients together. A very nice addition to our grilling repertoire. Too much work for the day of, so I recommend prepping the day before.

A very excellent Chicken sandwich! I read that people has issues with the mixture being too loose and the need to add more bread crumbs. I decided to leave out the tomato as I felt it would add to much moisture. The half cup bread crumbs is perfect. I added a slice of tomato on top of the patty after cooking. Very Very good!
Left out carrots but used the rest. Very moist burgers and now a family favourite
It was absolutly amazin

SO good. it’s a bit more work-intensive than your average burger, but definitely worth it. Juicy, tasty and the timing in the recipe is spot on. I did boost the old bay just a touch, and the combination of spices, salt, pepper, and sautéed veggies was wonderful without drowning out the flavor of the chicken. For the comments about it falling apart, if you watch the video, she makes a pretty tall burger I did the same, rolling them into a meatball and then flatteninto a tall patty, and it was just right.

Well.... My "Burger" like shape, kinda fell apart, but, it was delicious!! Also, I figure they fell apart because I didn't have fresh mushrooms so I used some canned I had on hand. I served them on toasted buns (We just ate them like sloppy joe's kinda haha) and we just loved them!!! Thank you so much for this recipe!!
Loved it, not very pretty but oh so delicious
So easy to put together and the taste was great! These burgers don't sit heavy. The cooking time is spot on.
Awesome!! I halved the recipe because it was just my wife and I, but now I want to make this for guests as well!! We didn't even use rolls or condiments! A definite keeper!

I halved the recipe and still made 8 burgers. I used Italian seasoning instead of Old Bay (which I only use for seafood). Next time I might add some cheese for more flavor. Overall, a good cow-burger alternative!
Added Tabasco sauce
